diff --git a/bandit/core/nosec.py b/bandit/core/nosec.py

index 0000000..bc64c69
--- /dev/null
+++ b/bandit/core/nosec.py
@@ -0,0 +1,420 @@
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Parsing of ``# nosec`` comments and suppression directives.
+
+Three directives complement the plain inline ``# nosec`` comment:
+
+``# nosec-begin [SELECTOR]``
+    Suppress findings on the lines following the directive.
+``# nosec-end``
+    End the most recently started region.
+``# nosec-next-line [SELECTOR]``
+    Suppress findings for the next statement.
+
+The optional selector limits a suppression to a set of tests, see
+:func:`resolve_selector` for the supported syntax.
+"""
+import collections
+import fnmatch
+import logging
+import re
+
+from bandit.core import extension_loader
+from bandit.core import utils
+
+LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# A plain inline suppression, i.e. ``# nosec`` or ``# nosec B602, B607``
+NOSEC_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s*nosec:?\s*(?P<tests>[^#]+)?#?")
+NOSEC_COMMENT_TESTS = re.compile(r"(?:(B\d+|[a-z\d_]+),?)+", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+# A region or next statement directive, i.e. ``# nosec-begin B602``
+NOSEC_DIRECTIVE_COMMENT = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-(?P<directive>begin|end|next-line)\b:?\s*(?P<selector>[^#]*)",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+BEGIN = "begin"
+END = "end"
+NEXT_LINE = "next-line"
+
+# Lines that are skipped when looking for the statement a next line
+# directive applies to: grouping tokens, semicolons and ellipsis literals
+# do not make up a statement of their own.
+CONTINUATION_LINE = re.compile(r"(?:[()\[\]{};]|\.\.\.|\s)+\Z")
+
+_SELECTOR_ATOM = re.compile(r"[\w.*?]+")
+_SELECTOR_OPERATORS = "|&-!()"
+_ATOM = "atom"
+_OP = "op"
+
+
+class _AllTests:
+    """Marker for a blanket suppression, one covering every test."""
+
+    def __repr__(self):
+        return "<all tests>"
+
+
+ALL_TESTS = _AllTests()
+
+
+class _SelectorError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a selector expression cannot be parsed."""
+
+
+_NOSEC_LINES = collections.namedtuple("NosecLines", ("suppressed", "inline"))
+
+
+class NosecLines(_NOSEC_LINES):
+    """The tests suppressed on each line of a file.
+
+    Both members map a line number to the set of tests suppressed for the
+    line, where an empty set means a blanket suppression.
+
+    :ivar suppressed: every suppression that applies to a line
+    :ivar inline: the suppressions coming from a plain ``# nosec`` comment,
+                  the only ones precise enough to report as unused
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ()
+
+
+def build_nosec_lines(lines, comments, test_ids):
+    """Build the suppressed tests for each line of a file.
+
+    :param lines: the physical lines of the file, as read from disk
+    :param comments: list of (line number, comment) tuples, in file order
+    :param test_ids: IDs of the tests that are enabled for this run
+    :return: the NosecLines of the file
+    """
+    nosec_lines = dict()
+    inline = dict()
+    if not comments:
+        return NosecLines(nosec_lines, inline)
+
+    directives = dict()
+    for lineno, comment in comments:
+        found = _parse_directive_comment(comment, test_ids)
+        if found:
+            directives.setdefault(lineno, []).extend(found)
+        tests = _parse_nosec_comment(_strip_directives(comment))
+        if tests is not None:
+            inline[lineno] = tests
+
+    def suppress(lineno, tests):
+        if tests is None or lineno is None:
+            return
+        nosec_lines[lineno] = utils.combine_nosec(
+            nosec_lines.get(lineno, None), tests
+        )
+
+    # regions are tracked as a stack of (indentation, tests) tuples, the
+    # innermost region last. An indentation of None marks a region that is
+    # not closed by a dedent.
+    regions = []
+    for lineno, line in enumerate(_decode_lines(lines) if directives else [], 1):
+        indent = _indentation(line)
+        if indent is not None:
+            # a dedent closes every region started further in
+            while regions and regions[-1][0] is not None:
+                if indent >= regions[-1][0]:
+                    break
+                regions.pop()
+
+        found = directives.get(lineno, [])
+        for directive, _ in found:
+            if directive == END and regions:
+                regions.pop()
+
+        for _, tests in regions:
+            suppress(lineno, tests)
+
+        for directive, tests in found:
+            if directive == BEGIN:
+                # a region begun on an unindented line cannot be dedented
+                # out of, only an end directive closes it
+                regions.append((indent or None, tests))
+            elif directive == NEXT_LINE:
+                suppress(_next_statement_line(lines, lineno), tests)
+
+    for lineno, tests in inline.items():
+        suppress(lineno, tests)
+
+    return NosecLines(nosec_lines, inline)
+
+
+def resolve_selector(selector, test_ids):
+    """Resolve a selector to the set of tests it suppresses.
+
+    A selector is a set expression over test IDs and test names. Tokens
+    separated by spaces or commas are unioned, as are those joined by ``|``.
+    The operators ``&`` (intersection), ``-`` (difference) and ``!``
+    (negation, relative to the enabled tests) are supported as well, and
+    parentheses may be used for grouping. A test ID may use a glob wildcard
+    to match several IDs by prefix, e.g. ``B6*``. The special token ``all``
+    selects every test, while ``none`` selects no test at all.
+
+    :param selector: the selector of a directive, may be empty
+    :param test_ids: IDs of the tests that are enabled for this run
+    :return: None when nothing is suppressed, an empty set for a blanket
+             suppression, or the set of tests to suppress
+    """
+    selector = selector.strip()
+    if not selector:
+        # a directive without selector suppresses every test
+        return set()
+
+    try:
+        tests = _parse_selector(selector, test_ids)
+    except _SelectorError as e:
+        LOG.debug("Unable to parse nosec selector %r: %s", selector, e)
+        # fall back to the plain union of all tokens in the selector
+        tests = set()
+        for token in re.split(r"[\s,]+", selector):
+            if token:
+                tests = _union(tests, _resolve_atom(token, test_ids))
+
+    if tests is ALL_TESTS:
+        return set()
+    return tests or None
+
+
+def _parse_directive_comment(comment, test_ids):
+    """Find the suppression directives in a comment.
+
+    :param comment: a comment, including its leading ``#``
+    :param test_ids: IDs of the tests that are enabled for this run
+    :return: list of (directive, tests to suppress) tuples, in comment order
+    """
+    directives = []
+    for match in NOSEC_DIRECTIVE_COMMENT.finditer(comment):
+        directive = match.group("directive").lower()
+        if directive == END:
+            # anything trailing an end directive is not a selector
+            directives.append((END, None))
+        else:
+            tests = resolve_selector(match.group("selector"), test_ids)
+            directives.append((directive, tests))
+    return directives
+
+
+def _strip_directives(comment):
+    """Remove any suppression directive from a comment."""
+    return NOSEC_DIRECTIVE_COMMENT.sub("", comment)
+
+
+def _parse_nosec_comment(comment):
+    found_no_sec_comment = NOSEC_COMMENT.search(comment)
+    if not found_no_sec_comment:
+        # there was no nosec comment
+        return None
+
+    matches = found_no_sec_comment.groupdict()
+    nosec_tests = matches.get("tests", set())
+
+    # empty set indicates that there was a nosec comment without specific
+    # test ids or names
+    test_ids = set()
+    if nosec_tests:
+        extman = extension_loader.MANAGER
+        # lookup tests by short code or name
+        for test in NOSEC_COMMENT_TESTS.finditer(nosec_tests):
+            test_match = test.group(1)
+            test_id = _find_test_id_from_nosec_string(extman, test_match)
+            if test_id:
+                test_ids.add(test_id)
+
+    return test_ids
+
+
+def _find_test_id_from_nosec_string(extman, match):
+    test_id = extman.check_id(match)
+    if test_id:
+        return match
+    # Finding by short_id didn't work, let's check the test name
+    test_id = extman.get_test_id(match)
+    if not test_id:
+        # Name and short id didn't work:
+        LOG.warning(
+            "Test in comment: %s is not a test name or id, ignoring", match
+        )
+    return test_id  # We want to return None or the string here regardless
+
+
+def _decode_lines(lines):
+    """Yield the given lines as text."""
+    for line in lines:
+        if isinstance(line, bytes):
+            line = line.decode("utf-8", "replace")
+        yield line
+
+
+def _indentation(line):
+    """Get the leading whitespace of a line, None if it is blank."""
+    stripped = line.lstrip()
+    if not stripped.strip():
+        return None
+    return len(line) - len(stripped)
+
+
+def _next_statement_line(lines, lineno):
+    """Find the first line of the statement following the given line.
+
+    Blank lines, comments and lines made up of grouping tokens only are
+    not statements of their own and therefore skipped.
+
+    :param lines: the physical lines of the file, as read from disk
+    :param lineno: the line number of the directive
+    :return: the line number of the statement, None if there is none
+    """
+    for offset, line in enumerate(_decode_lines(lines[lineno:]), start=1):
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        if (
+            not stripped
+            or stripped.startswith("#")
+            or CONTINUATION_LINE.match(stripped)
+        ):
+            continue
+        return lineno + offset
+    return None
+
+
+def _parse_selector(selector, test_ids):
+    """Parse and evaluate a selector expression."""
+    parser = _SelectorParser(_tokenize_selector(selector), test_ids)
+    return parser.parse()
+
+
+def _tokenize_selector(selector):
+    """Split a selector expression into atom and operator tokens."""
+    tokens = []
+    pos = 0
+    while pos < len(selector):
+        char = selector[pos]
+        if char.isspace() or char == ",":
+            # spaces and commas separate atoms to union
+            pos += 1
+        elif char in _SELECTOR_OPERATORS:
+            tokens.append((_OP, char))
+            pos += 1
+        else:
+            match = _SELECTOR_ATOM.match(selector, pos)
+            if match is None:
+                raise _SelectorError(f"unexpected character {char!r}")
+            tokens.append((_ATOM, match.group()))
+            pos = match.end()
+    if not tokens:
+        raise _SelectorError("no tests selected")
+    return tokens
+
+
+class _SelectorParser:
+    """A recursive descent parser for selector expressions."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tokens, test_ids):
+        self.tokens = tokens
+        self.test_ids = test_ids
+        self.pos = 0
+
+    def parse(self):
+        tests = self._union()
+        if self.pos != len(self.tokens):
+            raise _SelectorError(f"unexpected token {self._peek()[1]!r}")
+        return tests
+
+    def _peek(self):
+        return self.tokens[self.pos] if self.pos < len(self.tokens) else None
+
+    def _consume(self):
+        token = self._peek()
+        if token is None:
+            raise _SelectorError("unexpected end of selector")
+        self.pos += 1
+        return token
+
+    def _union(self):
+        tests = self._intersection()
+        while True:
+            token = self._peek()
+            if token is None:
+                break
+            if token == (_OP, "|"):
+                self._consume()
+            elif token[0] == _OP and token[1] not in "(!":
+                # an operator other than a group or negation ends the union
+                break
+            tests = _union(tests, self._intersection())
+        return tests
+
+    def _intersection(self):
+        tests = self._unary()
+        while True:
+            token = self._peek()
+            if token == (_OP, "&"):
+                self._consume()
+                tests = _intersection(tests, self._unary())
+            elif token == (_OP, "-"):
+                self._consume()
+                tests = _difference(tests, self._unary(), self.test_ids)
+            else:
+                return tests
+
+    def _unary(self):
+        if self._peek() == (_OP, "!"):
+            self._consume()
+            return _negation(self._unary(), self.test_ids)
+        return self._atom()
+
+    def _atom(self):
+        kind, value = self._consume()
+        if kind == _ATOM:
+            return _resolve_atom(value, self.test_ids)
+        if value == "(":
+            tests = self._union()
+            if self._peek() != (_OP, ")"):
+                raise _SelectorError("missing closing parenthesis")
+            self._consume()
+            return tests
+        raise _SelectorError(f"unexpected token {value!r}")
+
+
+def _resolve_atom(token, test_ids):
+    """Resolve a single selector token to the tests it selects."""
+    if token.lower() == "all":
+        return ALL_TESTS
+    if token.lower() == "none":
+        return set()
+    if "*" in token or "?" in token:
+        pattern = token.upper()
+        return {t for t in test_ids if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(t, pattern)}
+    test_id = _find_test_id_from_nosec_string(extension_loader.MANAGER, token)
+    return {test_id} if test_id else set()
+
+
+def _union(left, right):
+    if left is ALL_TESTS or right is ALL_TESTS:
+        return ALL_TESTS
+    return left | right
+
+
+def _intersection(left, right):
+    if left is ALL_TESTS:
+        return right
+    if right is ALL_TESTS:
+        return left
+    return left & right
+
+
+def _difference(left, right, test_ids):
+    if right is ALL_TESTS:
+        return set()
+    if left is ALL_TESTS:
+        return set(test_ids) - right
+    return left - right
+
+
+def _negation(tests, test_ids):
+    if tests is ALL_TESTS:
+        return set()
+    return set(test_ids) - tests

+def combine_nosec(first, second):
+    """Combine the tests suppressed by two nosec comments.
+
+    None means that no suppression applies, while an empty set means a
+    blanket suppression. A blanket suppression dominates any suppression
+    naming specific tests.
+
+    :param first: set of tests to suppress, or None
+    :param second: set of tests to suppress, or None
+    :return: the combined set of tests to suppress, or None
+    """
+    if first is None:
+        return second
+    if second is None:
+        return first
+    if not first or not second:
+        return set()
+    return first | second

   assert yaml.load("{}") == []  # nosec assert_used
 
+Suppressing a region of code
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+Repeating a ``# nosec`` comment on every line of a reviewed block of code can
+be avoided with the ``# nosec-begin`` and ``# nosec-end`` comments, which
+suppress the results of all the lines in between. The lines of the comments
+themselves are not suppressed.
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-begin
+  self.process = subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo', shell=True)
+  self.other = subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+  # nosec-end
+
+Regions may be nested and, just like a ``# nosec`` comment, the
+``# nosec-begin`` comment accepts the tests to suppress. A region that is not
+ended explicitly runs until the end of the file, or, when the
+``# nosec-begin`` comment is indented, until the first line indented less than
+the comment:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  def echo(self):
+      # nosec-begin B602
+      self.process = subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo', shell=True)
+
+  # the region above ended here, this is reported
+  self.other = subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+
+Suppressing the next statement
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+The ``# nosec-next-line`` comment suppresses the results of the statement
+following it, which is convenient when a line is too long already or when the
+statement spans several lines:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-next-line B602
+  self.process = subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo',
+                                  shell=True)
+
+Selecting the tests to suppress
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+The ``# nosec-begin`` and ``# nosec-next-line`` comments take an optional
+selector of the tests to suppress. Without one, or with the special ``all``
+token, every test is suppressed, while the special ``none`` token suppresses
+nothing. Tests are named by ID or by name, and IDs may use a glob wildcard to
+match by prefix:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-next-line B6*
+  self.process = subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+
+Tests separated by spaces or commas are suppressed together. The operators
+``|`` (union), ``&`` (intersection), ``-`` (difference) and ``!`` (every
+enabled test but those selected) are supported as well, and parentheses may be
+used for grouping:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-begin (B602, B607) & !start_process_with_partial_path
+  self.process = subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+  # nosec-end
+
+All of these comments are ignored when Bandit runs with ``--ignore-nosec``.
+

+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import io
+import textwrap
+import tokenize
+
+import testtools
+
+from bandit.core import nosec as b_nosec
+
+# a small set of enabled tests, enough to exercise the selector syntax
+TEST_IDS = frozenset(["B101", "B102", "B404", "B602", "B607"])
+
+BLANKET = set()
+
+
+def build_nosec_lines(source):
+    """Collect the nosec comments of a source snippet, as the manager does."""
+    data = textwrap.dedent(source).encode("utf-8")
+    comments = []
+    tokens = tokenize.tokenize(io.BytesIO(data).readline)
+    for toktype, tokval, (lineno, _), _, _ in tokens:
+        if toktype == tokenize.COMMENT:
+            comments.append((lineno, tokval))
+    return b_nosec.build_nosec_lines(data.splitlines(), comments, TEST_IDS)
+
+
+class SelectorTests(testtools.TestCase):
+    """This set of tests exercises the selectors of nosec directives."""
+
+    def resolve(self, selector):
+        return b_nosec.resolve_selector(selector, TEST_IDS)
+
+    def test_no_selector(self):
+        self.assertEqual(BLANKET, self.resolve(""))
+        self.assertEqual(BLANKET, self.resolve("   "))
+
+    def test_all_and_none(self):
+        self.assertEqual(BLANKET, self.resolve("all"))
+        self.assertEqual(BLANKET, self.resolve("ALL"))
+        self.assertIsNone(self.resolve("none"))
+        self.assertIsNone(self.resolve("None"))
+
+    def test_test_id(self):
+        self.assertEqual({"B602"}, self.resolve("B602"))
+
+    def test_test_name(self):
+        self.assertEqual({"B101"}, self.resolve("assert_used"))
+
+    def test_unknown_test(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(self.resolve("B999"))
+        self.assertIsNone(self.resolve("not_a_test"))
+        self.assertEqual({"B602"}, self.resolve("B602 not_a_test"))
+
+    def test_glob(self):
+        self.assertEqual({"B602", "B607"}, self.resolve("B6*"))
+        self.assertEqual({"B101", "B102"}, self.resolve("b10?"))
+        self.assertEqual(set(TEST_IDS), self.resolve("B*"))
+
+    def test_separators(self):
+        expected = {"B101", "B602"}
+        self.assertEqual(expected, self.resolve("B101 B602"))
+        self.assertEqual(expected, self.resolve("B101,B602"))
+        self.assertEqual(expected, self.resolve("B101, assert_used, B602"))
+
+    def test_operators(self):
+        self.assertEqual({"B101", "B602"}, self.resolve("B101 | B602"))
+        self.assertEqual({"B602"}, self.resolve("B6* & B602"))
+        self.assertEqual(set(), self.resolve("B101 & B602") or set())
+        self.assertEqual({"B607"}, self.resolve("B6* - B602"))
+        self.assertEqual(TEST_IDS - {"B602"}, self.resolve("!B602"))
+        self.assertEqual({"B602"}, self.resolve("!!B602"))
+        self.assertEqual(set(TEST_IDS), self.resolve("!none"))
+        self.assertIsNone(self.resolve("!all"))
+
+    def test_operators_with_all(self):
+        self.assertEqual(BLANKET, self.resolve("all | B602"))
+        self.assertEqual({"B602"}, self.resolve("all & B602"))
+        self.assertEqual(TEST_IDS - {"B602"}, self.resolve("all - B602"))
+
+    def test_grouping(self):
+        self.assertEqual({"B607"}, self.resolve("(B101 | B607) & B6*"))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {"B101", "B607"}, self.resolve("B101 | (B6* - B602)")
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            TEST_IDS - {"B101", "B607"}, self.resolve("!(B101 | B6* - B602)")
+        )
+
+    def test_unparsable_selector_falls_back_to_a_union(self):
+        self.assertEqual({"B101", "B602"}, self.resolve("B101 & | B602"))
+        # the tokens of the union that are no test are ignored
+        self.assertEqual({"B602"}, self.resolve("(B101 B602"))
+        self.assertIsNone(self.resolve("&"))
+
+
